title: Deeper/broader NOD entry ordering and keyed-closure contract
mode: Primary-source web research and local plan reconciliation; plan-only
scope: Resolve whether ordinal order of entries inside the regenerated DXF Named Object Dictionary is a format-semantic parity requirement.
Separate first-OBJECTS-record root identity from repeated dictionary key/handle pairs.
Refine existing 7G generated-test expectations without reducing root-entry closure requirements.

sources.observed: The DICTIONARY schema uses repeated entry-name and handle pairs. Autodesk's OBJECTS example identifies the named-object dictionary as the first OBJECTS object. The ActiveX model describes dictionary retrieval by keyword.
sources.limits: The reviewed pages do not explicitly state that entry ordinal order is semantically irrelevant; absence of an order rule is not universal consumer proof.

sources.revision: Mutable stable documentation accessed 2026-10-20; no executable run
sources.observed: The API describes dictionary key/entity pairs, case-insensitive AutoCAD keys, second-stage handle resolution, and root keys by name and target role.
sources.limits: Documentation/source behavior is peer implementation evidence, not a normative DXF statement or independent interoperability run.

sources.revision: Mutable master source accessed 2026-10-20; no executable run or immutable commit pinned
sources.observed: The dictionary lookup helper scans entries and selects the one whose name matches the requested key; NOD discovery separately identifies the first DICTIONARY object.
sources.limits: This corroborates keyed lookup in one peer, but does not establish behavior for every consumer or amend the format contract.

sources.observed: The writer regenerates fixed root entries and emits supplied entries; strict adapter export admits known target families by key/identity and rejects unsupported or incomplete routes according to existing gates. ACAD_LAYOUT may be regenerated outside its source position.
sources.limits: No code path or generated file was executed in this research pass; local source inspection is not consumer acceptance.

existingSubplansRefined: 7G: retain strict NOD-first OBJECTS placement, assess entry closure by normalized key-to-target identity, and treat ordinal output order as deterministic serialization rather than a semantic support claim
PAR-49: generated root graph controls verify key uniqueness, target type/owner reciprocity, remapped identity, and payload reachability independently of entry order

planChanges: Separated the normative physical placement requirement for the NOD (first OBJECTS record) from ordinal order of repeated NOD key/handle entries.
Reframed root-entry effective order as deterministic serializer behavior, not a support/parity gate; no claim is made that all consumers ignore order.
Kept full source root closure, duplicate-key rejection, target-family identity, reciprocal ownership, remapping, and fail-closed publication as open implementation requirements.
Specified that exact ordered assertions remain appropriate for independently defined sequences such as LAYOUT viewport handles and SORTENTSTABLE pairs.
limitations: The DXF sources reviewed do not contain an explicit normative statement declaring NOD entry order semantically irrelevant.
No peer implementation was built or executed; code lookup behavior is corroborative only.
This resolves the wording of one 7G sub-question and does not close remaining root-entry target-family or reciprocity gaps.
